answer: Admission tolls that rise with the gale: every new identity pays a joining fee scaled to the network's own registration velocity. When a registration storm blows, tolls multiply like dock fees at a crowded jetty, making mass sybil insertion ruinously expensive while patient newcomers wait for calm seas. Tolls are burned, and part funds the investigators who hunt farms, so each fake pays both the fee and the bounty on its own head. Honest joiners ride out the weather like lotus, paying once; a farmer must buy N tolls at storm prices. Cost grows with N and with the attack's own speed.
